# frontend

<!-- layer1:start · generated by the harness · do not edit by hand -->

## Verification

1. **Verify before asserting, and with whatever consumes it.** Never take a
   file's word about the environment: **run the tool that reads it and trigger
   what it controls.** What cannot be checked stays `❓ pending`, said out loud.

   _Asking is not enough: `pnpm config get` answered `42` for a key that does
   not exist, and `true` for one that changed nothing._

2. **"Done" means verified by CI, not asserted.** What has not passed the gate
   stays pending, and that is said.

   _A green on your machine only proves your machine._

## What the AI does not decide

3. **`.env`, credentials and real data dumps: neither read without explicit
   permission, nor committed.** What the agent reads **enters the
   conversation**, and from there it does not come back. `.env.example` is what
   travels.

4. **The AI installs and configures nothing on its own**: it proposes, the owner
   decides.

   _An install or a config change lands in everyone's lockfile and CI, and
   neither shows in the diff the agent presents._

5. **Nothing destructive without a `--dry-run` first**, showing what would be
   deleted.

   _A `git clean -fd` took three unrecoverable directories._

6. **The AI commits; the person decides the push.** Local commits pile up until
   the go-ahead, **and one go-ahead covers one push**, not the next ones.

7. **No AI trace in commits or output**: no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated
   with…".

   _Tools add it by default. History says what changed and why, not with which
   tool._

8. **Conventional Commits, in English**: `type(scope): summary`, with `!` for a
   breaking change. The types: `feat` · `fix` · `docs` · `style` · `refactor` ·
   `perf` · `test` · `build` · `ci` · `chore` · `revert`. The body carries
   **only** the list of changes and the reason for each — the how is already in
   the diff.

## The environment

9. **An agent session has no Node auto-switch.** The hook lives in the shell
   profile and a non-interactive session never loads it: the session runs on
   whatever Node it **inherited when it was launched**, and `cd` into another
   project does not change it.

   **Start the session from a terminal already on the repo's version** — enter
   the directory, let fnm/nvm switch, then launch the agent. **One session per
   project.**

   _If that was not done, activate it on every invocation: `fnm use <major>`
   then the command. `fnm exec --using=N pnpm` does not work on Windows — `pnpm`
   is a `.cmd` and `fnm exec` only launches real executables._

10. **pnpm, never npm.**

_`npm install` leaves a `package-lock.json` next to `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and two
installers disagree in silence._

11. **pnpm settings live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`**; `.npmrc` carries registry
    and authentication only — from pnpm 11 anything else there is ignored, and
    pnpm 10 still reads it, so it works today and stops on upgrade. Every repo
    with dependencies sets `minimumReleaseAge` there.

## Continuity

12. **State lives in `docs/SESSION.md`**, written **when a task closes** — at
    session close there is no context left — and **overwritten**: git keeps the
    history. Nothing the code or `git log` already tells goes in.

13. **The reasoning lives in `docs/DECISIONS.md`**, append-only. A decision that
    changes **is not edited**: another is appended revising it, and the old one
    is **marked, never deleted**. Knowing what was believed is part of the
    record.

14. **An exception is declared** in the project's `AGENTS.md`, with its reason
    and its scope; failing silently is not an option. Does not apply to
    security, AI traces or pushing.

## Naming

15. **File names, configuration keys and identifiers in English.**

## Knowledge that is not in this file

16. **Skills are per project.** `npx autoskills` installs them into
    `<repo>/.claude/skills/`, which is **git-ignored and rebuilt** like
    `node_modules`; **`skills-lock.json` is committed** — it carries each
    skill's source and hash, and it is what makes three machines rebuild the
    same set. **The developer runs `autoskills`, not the agent** — `npx`
    downloads a package, and installing is not the agent's call.

_Global skills in `~/.claude/skills/` are the machine's, not the project's._

17. **Official docs and MCPs are consulted and never silenced**, at the
    **installed** version — from the lockfile, not the `^` range. **Context7 is
    the one every project uses**: `resolve-library-id`, then `query-docs` at
    that version. If the MCP does not answer, say so instead of pretending it
    was consulted.

## Review

18. **When work is reviewed, this is the shape.** `architect` before building;
    `reviewer` and `security` over what was built, **read-only**; `tester` to
    verify. Run them whenever you want, together or on their own.

<!-- layer1:end -->

`frontend/` is one of two independent pnpm projects inside the `Four-Points`
repo (the other is `backend/`). The root [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) holds what
both share — Context7 policy, Markdown formatting, commits and hooks, the
security level, the frontend ↔ backend contract and the module map — and is
loaded through the root `CLAUDE.md`.

This file also covers the stack, commands, architecture and module docs of
`frontend/`. Paths are relative to `frontend/` unless they start with
`backend/`.

## Exceptions

- **Rules 12 and 13 — state and decisions live at the repo root.** They are
  `docs/SESSION.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md` in the root, shared with `backend/`.
  `frontend/docs/` is git-ignored (`frontend/.gitignore:85`) and is not used for
  them.

## Security

**L3** — estimated on 2026-09-28: there is login and user accounts, personal
data (users, guest blacklist with photos, cashier) and own backend; the L3 level
is declared by the owner as the target (`docs/DECISIONS.md` ADR-017), not the
current state. **Re-estimate when:** Aiven starts storing real guest or staff
data.

The level line is the same in the root `AGENTS.md` and in `backend/AGENTS.md`; a
re-estimate changes all three. Paths below are relative to `frontend/`.

**Areas:**

- Authentication, Session → `app/lib/auth/` (`useAuth.tsx`, `authService.ts`,
  `passwordPolicy.ts`), `app/(auth)/login/`, `proxy.ts` (route protection; reads
  the JWT `exp` without verifying it), `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` (redirect)
- Authorization → UI gating only: `app/ui/dashboard/nav-links.tsx`,
  `app/ui/dashboard/sidenav.tsx`, `app/dashboard/scheduling/layout.tsx`;
  enforcement lives in the backend
- API → `app/lib/apiClient.ts`, `app/lib/serverFetch.ts`, per-module calls in
  `app/lib/<module>/`, server actions in `app/dashboard/blacklist/actions/`
- File upload → client side, under `app/components/`:
  `blacklist/ui/ImageUploader.tsx`, `bo/modals/PdfUploadModal.tsx`, the
  maintenance and groups panels, `restaurant/tabs/DailyRevenueTab.tsx`
- Data protection / privacy → blacklist, cashier, users
  (`app/components/auth/NewUserModal.tsx`, profile) and messaging
  (`app/components/profile/MessagesPanel.tsx`, `app/lib/messaging/`)
- Frontend → `next.config.ts` (CSP and security headers), `react-markdown` in
  `app/components/checklist/` over `content/checklist/`,
  `app/components/blacklist/ui/Highlight.tsx`
- Configuration / DevOps → `next.config.ts`, `vercel.json`, `app/lib/env.ts`,
  `.env*`

## Where the model goes wrong

- **A prompt that asks for several tasks at once** → work them **one at a
  time**, each with the context specific to it, when the work touches code.

## Stack

- **Next.js 16** (App Router, Turbopack in dev) with **React 19**, on Node 24
  (`.nvmrc`, `engines: 24.x`), pnpm 10.28.0. TypeScript 5.7.3.
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS **v3**; UI from NextUI (`@nextui-org`), Headless UI,
  Heroicons and `react-icons`.
- **State**: Zustand stores in `app/stores/`; server data through React Query.
- **Forms**: React Hook Form + Zod **v3**.
- **i18n**: `next-intl`. **Theme**: `next-themes`. PDFs with `pdf-lib` and
  `pdfjs-dist`, charts with `recharts`, spreadsheets with `xlsx`.
- No auth library: `next-auth`, `bcrypt`, `mysql2`, `postgres` and `uuid` were
  removed on 2026-10-02 as unused.

- **`typescript`** 5.7.3 — `backend/` runs 5.9.3

## Commands

```bash
pnpm dev              # Next.js dev server with Turbopack (port 3000)
pnpm build            # production bundle
pnpm start            # production server
pnpm lint             # ESLint
pnpm typecheck        # tsc --noEmit
pnpm format           # Prettier (format:check to only check)
pnpm verify           # lint + format:check + typecheck — what CI runs
```

There is no test suite in `frontend/`.

## Architecture

```
app/
├── (auth)/          # login
├── dashboard/       # protected routes, one folder per module
├── components/      # UI per module (components/<module>/)
├── lib/             # apiClient, serverFetch, env, auth/, and lib/<module>/
├── stores/          # Zustand stores
├── i18n/            # next-intl config and locale resolution
└── ui/              # design system: dashboard shell, fonts, tokens, global.css
messages/<locale>/   # translations, one JSON per namespace
content/checklist/   # checklist guides rendered by the app
proxy.ts             # route protection
```

- **Everything lives under `app/`** — there is **no `frontend/lib/`**; the
  utilities directory is `app/lib/`.
- **Server components by default.** `'use client'` only when the component has
  interactivity, uses React hooks or browser APIs. Never `useState` in a server
  component, never an `async` client component.
- **Data fetching**: client components use React Query with
  `app/lib/apiClient.ts`; server components use `app/lib/serverFetch.ts`. A few
  modules also have server actions (`app/dashboard/<module>/actions/`,
  `app/lib/parking/actions.ts`).
- **Every call carries `credentials: 'include'`** — `apiClient` adds it, and
  retries once through `/api/auth/refresh-token` on a 401.
- **Environment**: all API URLs come from `app/lib/env.ts` —
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (browser), `NEXT_SERVER_API_URL` (server, falls back to
  the public one) and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_MODE`. Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` reaches the
  browser.
- **Forms**: React Hook Form + Zod; schemas live with their module
  (`app/lib/<module>/`, plus `app/lib/schemas/` for groups).
- **Theme**: `next-themes` (`app/lib/theme/ThemeProvider.tsx`) toggles the
  `.dark` class on `<html>`.
- **Fonts**: configured in `app/ui/fonts-design/`; the active set is
  `ACTIVE_FONTS` in `fonts.helper.ts`, applied with `font-sans` and
  `font-display`.

### i18n

`next-intl` v4 with locales `es` and `en`. The locale is resolved in
`app/i18n/request.ts`: cookie `NEXT_LOCALE`, then Vercel's
`x-vercel-ip-country`, then `Accept-Language`, default `es`. No `routing.ts` and
no locale in the URL. Messages in `messages/<locale>/<namespace>.json`.

## Authentication and Route Protection

The contract with the backend is in the root `AGENTS.md`; here, the frontend
side.

- **`app/lib/auth/useAuth.tsx`** — the `AuthProvider` calls `GET /api/auth/me`
  on mount; `useAuth()` (alias `useAuthContext`) gives `user`, `login`, `logout`
  and `isAuthenticated`.
- **`proxy.ts`** redirects by the presence and `exp` of the JWT cookie,
  **without verifying it**; `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` redirects when
  `useAuth()` has no user. Real enforcement is the backend's.
- ⚠️ **There is no dev-mode auth bypass.** Older docs mentioned a `DEV_MODE`
  flag and a `DashboardLayout` component: neither exists. Do not write code that
  assumes auth can be skipped locally.
- Role checks in the UI only hide navigation and screens.

## Messaging

No module doc yet. ⚠️ **There is no `app/dashboard/messages/` route**: the UI is
a panel inside the profile page, `app/components/profile/MessagesPanel.tsx`,
with hooks and queries in `app/lib/messaging/`. The backend side is in
`backend/AGENTS.md` § Messaging.
